content: Steri-Strips are adhesive-backed surgical paper tapes designed to be applied across incisions or minor cuts. Their primary function is to hold the edges of a wound together during the healing process. These strips were developed by the company 3M and are often used as an alternative to sutures (stitches) in certain injuries. This is because they are associated with reduced scarring and are generally easier to manage compared to traditional sutures. The development of Steri-Strips was inspired by the earlier use of Micropore Surgical Tape. There are documented cases where Micropore Surgical Tape was successfully used to manage significant wounds. For instance, it was employed to hold together large abdominal incisions in patients whose skin was too fragile to tolerate sutures. In one remarkable case, the tape was used to reconstruct a patient’s abdominal wall and save their life when sutures failed to hold due to compromised skin integrity. Steri-Strips are not suitable for use over joints, as the movement in these areas can compromise their effectiveness. However, they are particularly useful in regions where the skin is thin and there is a risk of sutures cutting through the tissue. To enhance the adhesive properties of Steri-Strips, tincture of benzoin can be applied to the dry skin surrounding the wound before application.
